slides.hook: When a split lands between a question and its reply, search finds the question and loses the answer. Open each chunk at a question.
inside: Where a size split separates question and answer
Exchange chunks with the call and time on top
Long answers: the question on every piece
Hidden questions, and when to move on

slides.title: Chunk by / [exchange]
slides.text: A call is a run of speaker turns, and an answer reads as one only next to the question before it.

steps: Merge caption lines into one line per speaker turn.
Keep the speaker label and timestamp on every turn.
Open a new chunk at each question; run it to the next one.
Put the call title and the time range on top.
An exchange over the limit: split the answer, repeat the question on each piece.

slides.title: Search finds / the [question]

slides.title: Turn separators / still [pack]
slides.text: A timestamp regex as the first separator, same `chunk_size=300`:
bullets: 4 chunks. Chunks 2 and 3 still end on a question, and the answers open the next chunk.
The splitter packs whole turns up to 300 characters, whether or not a question has its answer yet.

slides.title: When a question / [hides]
slides.text: A first version tested `t.endswith("?")`. Change one turn to "Which plan is the account on? I can check." and compare:

options.output: "Starter, I think." filed under "How can I help?"

bullets: Caption files (WebVTT) cut one turn into short timed cues. Merge lines from the same speaker first.
"Speaker 1" labels: map them to names or roles before indexing.
Speech-to-text output without punctuation has no "?" to match: restore punctuation first.

cards.title: Use it when
items: Support calls, interviews and meetings with speaker labels
Questions get asked and answered in the call
Answers must cite a speaker and a timestamp

cards.title: Move on when
items: No speaker labels: run speaker diarization first
One speaker talks for most of the recording: split by topic
Questions cover the whole call: summaries per call
Clarifying questions come before the answer: group by topic

slides.title: [Cheat] sheet
rows: One line per speaker turn, with label and timestamp
Open a new chunk at each question
Title and time range on top of every chunk
Long answer: split at sentences, repeat the question
Match "?" anywhere in a turn; check your transcripts keep question marks
Merge caption cues from the same speaker first

slides.line: A chunk pulled out of a long call or document can lose what "that limit" refers to. Next: give each chunk a short context before embedding.
